chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Deputy Chief and Acting Chief
paragraphs: (a) There shall be a Deputy Chief of the United States Capitol Police, who shall serve as the principal subordinate officer to the Chief and shall assist in the administration, command, supervision, discipline, training, recordkeeping, staffing, and daily operation of the Capitol Police.
(b) The Deputy Chief shall be appointed by the Chief.

(c) The Deputy Chief shall serve at the pleasure of the Chief. The Chief may remove, replace, reassign, suspend, or limit the duties of the Deputy Chief at any time, with or without cause, subject only to this Act and any generally applicable employment laws governing the Capitol Police or the Government in general.

(d) The Deputy Chief shall perform such duties as are assigned by the Chief, including duties relating to patrol operations, protective services, officer supervision, training, emergency response, records, internal discipline, interagency coordination, access control, and enforcement of regulations issued under this Act.

(e) The Chief may delegate any operational or administrative duty of the Capitol Police to the Deputy Chief, except that no delegation shall relieve the Chief of responsibility to the Board or authorize the Deputy Chief to exercise authority greater than that possessed by the Chief.
(f) The Deputy Chief shall remain subject to the authority, direction, and supervision of the Chief in all ordinary operations of the Capitol Police.

(g) If the Chief is absent, disabled, removed, resigned, unreachable, vacant, or otherwise unable to discharge the duties of the office, the Deputy Chief shall serve as Acting Chief unless the Capitol Police Board designates another officer of the Capitol Police to serve as Acting Chief.

(h) An Acting Chief shall possess the powers and duties of the Chief only for the period necessary to preserve command continuity, respond to emergencies, maintain operations, and carry out the lawful duties of the Capitol Police until the Chief resumes duty, a successor is appointed, or the Board provides otherwise.

(i) While serving as Acting Chief, the Deputy Chief may issue temporary operational orders, direct officers and employees, respond to emergencies, maintain security operations, request emergency assistance, and carry out any duty necessary to prevent interruption of Capitol Police operations.

(j) No Acting Chief may enter into a permanent interagency agreement, permanently alter the command structure of the Capitol Police, issue a major regulation of continuing effect, remove or appoint senior command staff on a permanent basis, or substantially change the jurisdiction, policies, or long-term operations of the Capitol Police without approval of the Board, except where immediate action is necessary to respond to an emergency.
(k) Any major action taken by an Acting Chief during an emergency shall be reported to the Board as soon as practicable after the emergency permits.

(l) Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the authority of the Chief to appoint, remove, supervise, direct, or assign duties to the Deputy Chief, except when the Deputy Chief is serving as Acting Chief under this section.

sections.heading: Jurisdiction of the United States Capitol Police
paragraphs: (a) The Capitol Police shall have primary law enforcement and protective jurisdiction within the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds.

(b) The jurisdiction of the Capitol Police shall include the United States Capitol, the Hall of the House of Representatives, the Senate Chamber, congressional offices, committee rooms, hearing rooms, galleries, cloakrooms, corridors, entrances, exits, ceremonial rooms and exterior grounds.

(c) The Capitol Police may exercise jurisdiction over any building, room, facility, platform, exterior area, or temporary location used for official congressional business when such location is acquired, leased, reserved, designated, or otherwise placed under the protection of the Capitol Police by the Board, the Speaker, the President pro tempore, the Sergeant at Arms of either House, or another lawful authority acting under the rules of either House.

(d) Within its jurisdiction, the Capitol Police may preserve order, protect persons and property, prevent obstruction of congressional business, regulate access as authorized by law or rule, enforce lawful security regulations, enforce the laws of the United States, respond to emergencies, investigate violations of law, remove persons as authorized by this Act, detain persons as authorized by this Act, and make arrests for violations of law.

(e) The Capitol Police may exercise temporary jurisdiction outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds when necessary to protect a Member of Congress, officer of Congress, congressional employee, witness, invited guest, or other person connected to official congressional business.

(f) The Capitol Police may exercise temporary jurisdiction outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds when an area is being used for an official congressional hearing, meeting, inspection, ceremony, investigation, proceeding, delegation, conference, or other official function of Congress or either House.

(g) The Capitol Police may exercise temporary jurisdiction outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds when providing protective services authorized under this Act, transporting or escorting a protected person, responding to an imminent threat against Congress, assisting another law enforcement agency during an emergency, or carrying out a lawful order of the Board or the relevant Sergeant at Arms.

(h) Temporary jurisdiction outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds shall last only as long as necessary to carry out the congressional purpose, protective assignment, emergency response, escort, transport, investigation, or authorized operation that justified the temporary jurisdiction.

(i) The temporary jurisdiction provided by this section is intended to be narrower than a general law-enforcement jurisdiction and shall be construed only as authority necessary to protect Congress, congressional proceedings, congressional functions, congressional facilities, protected persons, official congressional business, or emergency operations connected to Congress.

(j) The Capitol Police shall not exercise temporary jurisdiction outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds solely because a federal offense has occurred, solely because a person involved is a federal officer or employee, solely because an outside law-enforcement agency requests general assistance, or solely because the matter is of public importance, unless the matter is also connected to Congress, congressional security, official congressional business, a protected person, an official congressional function, emergency assistance authorized by this Act, or another lawful basis expressly recognized by this Act.

(k) Nothing in this section shall prevent the Capitol Police from assisting another law-enforcement agency during an emergency, protecting a person covered by this Act, preserving evidence connected to a threat against Congress, responding to fresh pursuit from Capitol Police jurisdiction, or taking temporary action necessary to prevent death, serious bodily injury, active violence, or an imminent threat involving Congress or a protected person.

(l) The Chief shall maintain records of any exercise of temporary jurisdiction outside the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, including the location, purpose, duration, officers involved, authority relied upon, and whether any arrest, detention, use of force, injury, property damage, or outside agency assistance occurred. (m)Any exercise of temporary jurisdiction involving a major security incident, arrest, detention, use of force, deployment of multiple officers, or assistance from an outside law enforcement agency shall be reported to the Capitol Police Board as soon as practicable.
